messages:
ashley: FYI - Dependabot flagged CVE-2026-12345 in our httpx fork. It looks exploitable via a transitive KMS client path. Repro attached.
ben: can you paste the minimal repro here? want to see if this affects hosted API path or only private deploys
ashley: repro snippet:
```
# flow: client -> kms-proxy -> httpx lib
headers leaking = True
requests.get('https://metadata.internal', headers=user_headers)
```
ashley: that shows the issue with header forwarding in the transitive lib. Seems low probability in hosted (no metadata access) but higher for private on-prem and VPCs with metadata endpoints.
carla: what's the CVSS and public exploitability? any PoC published?
ashley: CVSS 7.2, no public PoC yet. Reported to upstream yesterday. They marked it "high" due to header leak pattern.
elaine: SLA question: if this becomes public, customers on Dedicated/Private expect a fast patch. How long until a safe patch/rollback path?
ben: we can push a patch to our shim (filter headers) within 24-48h. Rolling patch across Dedicated pools will take longer due to approval windows - estimate 72h for full Dedicated rollout if we do staging -> canary -> all.
sre-oncall: timeline sounds plausible. Need to reserve maintenance windows for sensitive customer tiers (enterprise customers on contracts). We should avoid mass restarts during peak APAC times.
carla: proposal: staggered schedule - immediate emergency hotfix for Hosted (filter at edge), simultaneous mitigation config for Dedicated (rate-limit + extra header strip via nginx), then full library upgrade in next weekly patch window for Private.
elaine: +1. Also prepare customer comms for Tier 1 (SLA) within 24h and Tier 2 in 48h. Include suggested mitigations they can apply (network ACLs, metadata hardening).
ashley: ops-bot: create incident ticket and assign to ben + carla + infra team
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-045 created by ashley. Priority: P1. Assignees: ben, carla. SLA impact flagged: possible for Dedicated/Private only.
ben: quick mitigation patch (nginx header filter) ready, testing now. If tests pass, I'll push to staging canary in ~1h.
carla: I'll draft customer notice, include workaround steps and timeline. Ping me if the canary fails.
sre-oncall: add rollback playbook: if latency spikes >5% or error rate >1% within 15m after deploy, auto rollback. Also open capacity buffer for failover.
ashley: approved. Ben, push canary; label PR with "security/urgent" and include CVE ref. After canary looks good, we schedule Dedicated staggered rollout during regional low-traffic windows.
ben: canary passed basic tests. Starting canary deploy to 5% of Hosted and one Dedicated cluster.
carla: drafting email for Tier 1 customers: short note, impact: possible header leak on Private/Dedicated if metadata endpoints reachable; mitigation: apply our patch/remove host metadata access; timeline: hotfix applied to Hosted now, Dedicated staggered over 72h, Private next maintenance cycle. Will post to portal.
elaine: also loop in legal and compliance for required disclosure timeline if PoC appears. Contact: legal@redwood.com
ashley: follow-ups: (1) add audit log entry for header-filter rollouts, (2) update RBAC so only infra role can toggle mitigation, (3) schedule postmortem once fully resolved.
ops-bot: note added to INC-2026-045: audit-log required, RBAC change request created (REQ-2026-89).
ben: rolling to Dedicated stage 1 now. I'll report back after 30m checks.
carla: thanks. I'll update #status-security with customer communication snippets and a draft post to status.redwood.com
sre-oncall: keeping alerting on. If we see any customer reports, escalate immediately to SE oncall and PM.
ashley: closing loop: no public exploit yet, mitigation in place for Hosted, Dedicated staggered, Private scheduled. Filing follow-up eval for dependency upgrade to prevent recurrence. Thanks team :heart:
